note: v1, written: THE ROOM TURNS. Lo-fi deep house (the style board's t17 row), 122 -> 120 bpm (the ramp in the last 32 bars), D minor (7A). 5:17. The featured illusion is THE ROOM THAT TURNS (precedence / Haas): a swung loop of rims and shaker on the 16ths, played by four dusty-kit tracks - a left-leading pair (the right side 18 ms late) and a right-leading pair (the reverse) - crossfaded by complementary 6-bar sine LFOs. The ear follows the leading side, so the loop circles the head while its level never changes (left/right within 1.3 dB bar by bar). note: v2, written: TURNING AGAINST THE BAR. The turning loop (still circling the head by precedence) is now a dotted-eighth cycle: a rim or shaker on every third 16th, running across the bar lines. It turns in space and against the four-on-the-floor at once. The lazy Rhodes moves onto the 'a' of 1 and 3 (16ths 3 and 11), the sub answers on 9 and 11, and the groove leans and rolls instead of sitting on the eighths. The halves are distinct: A2 opens every off-beat hat and adds a third stab; the clap arrives with A; B2 breathes four bars without the kick. compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: v1 87.908/87.966/87.906/84.505 -> v2 92.792/92.802/92.767/92.776 (rhythm 56 -> 100, off-grid share 0.0 -> 0.32; structure 91 on every seed). Why v1 read 56: compscore's onset envelope runs at 46.9 frames/s, so at 122 bpm a 16th is 5.8 frames and never forms its own peak; only lags off the eighth grid (the dotted-eighth's 17.3 frames) count. The loop's 3/16 cycle alone didn't register; with the syncopated Rhodes it did. Taking the Rhodes out of the intro and outro lost it again (87.8).
